extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and practitioners in political communication, media studies, and computational social science
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and implementing measurement and analysis procedures to quantify partisan segregation in online news consumption (audience- and content-level), and to link media diets to attitudinal change during an election campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolation index (domain-level partisan segregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Isolation index = average Republican audience share of web visits made by Republicans minus the average Republican audience share of web visits made by Democrats; bounded between zero and one with intuitive interpretations (0 = no partisan isolation; 1 = complete segregation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute using visits aggregated to the unique daily visit (indicator for whether a panelist visited the news domain at least once on a given day) to mirror Gentzkow and Shapiro (2011). Use sample weights to weight the panel back to a nationally representative sample. An adjusted version of the isolation index is used to correct for bias when the number of visitors to a web domain is small (formula in Appendix D). Compare indices across years or domain subsets for benchmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaled standard deviation of partisan news exposure (Ri / Flaxman et al. measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each individual i compute Ri = (1/Ni) Σ_{j=1..Ni} r(dij), where Ni is number of URLs on news domains visited by i, dij is the domain of jth URL, and r(d) is the Republican share of domain d. The segregation measure is the scaled standard deviation of Ri across individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this alternative measure to compare segregation to prior work (e.g., Flaxman et al., 2016). It operationalizes individual-level exposure by averaging domain partisan composition across an individual's visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience composition by domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of a domain's overall pageviews coming from Democrats, Republicans, and independents (including leaners with the party they are closest to).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report party shares for top domains to characterize partisan audience composition (e.g., Table 1). Use these shares to illustrate partisan ordering of high-traffic websites and validate correspondence with other measures (content-based slant, Facebook sharing patterns, ComScore, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content focus categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify each election-related article by topical focus: issue positions (policy), campaign events (event), political horse race or campaign strategy (strategy), scandal coverage (moral, legal, or financial wrongdoing), or other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop coding scheme iteratively on a small sample; provide coder training and validation. Use these categories to assess how partisan isolation varies across types of coverage (e.g., scandals vs policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partisan slant coding (five-point scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coders evaluate the net partisan slant of news reports on a five-point scale: (1) clearly more favorable to Democrats, (3) even-handed/neutral, (5) clearly more favorable to Republicans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to test partisan selectivity by slant at the article level. Note measurement difficulty: low inter-coder reliability measures in pre-test (r = 0.23, κ = 0.07), with primary tension about neutral vs non-neutral classification; when both coders labeled as non-neutral they agreed on direction 80% of the time. Aggregate site-level averages correspond strongly to partisan audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdsourced content analysis reliability procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Amazon Mechanical Turk coders; develop coding scheme iteratively; require coders to complete a political knowledge quiz before evaluating articles; cap the number of articles per coder at 200; validate coding scheme via pre-tests with multiple coders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main analysis labels each article based on one coder, but conduct validation on subsets rated by multiple coders to assess inter-coder correspondence and measurement error. Report reliability statistics and discuss implications for article-level slant measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of election-related news for content selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Election-related news defined as stories that mentioned 'Clinton' or 'Trump' in the first hundred words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply a concrete textual rule to identify articles for the election-focused content analysis (yielded 55,000 election-related stories out of 212,000 unique news articles read).

rubrics_metrics.name: Web browsing measurement via passive tracking toolbar
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure web browsing behavior using the Wakoopa toolbar installed by respondents; passively track number of visits to web domains and particular URLs between August 1 and November 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: removes measurement error from self-reports. Concerns: low uptake of toolbar (selection bias). Address via survey weights, alternative raking weights (e.g., based on political interest), and validation checks (compare aggregate traffic to ComScore). Report uptake/completion rates and account for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of news domains for scraping
rubrics_metrics.description: Scrape pages from a set of 355 politically focused news domains composed of: the top 100 web domains for news based on overall traffic among panelists and an additional 255 US-based websites from the Alexa most popular news domains list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mainstream newspapers, television outlets, web aggregators, and online-only news sites. Report domain list (Appendix G) and note coverage proportion (1.1 million visits; 4% of overall visits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of analysis choice: unique daily visit
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate visit-level data to the unique daily visit (an indicator for whether a panelist visited the news domain at least once on a given day) when computing isolation index to mirror prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly match units to earlier studies (Gentzkow & Shapiro) for comparability. Acknowledge that this measure captures audience composition but not within-person variety of exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted isolation index bias correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an adjusted version of the isolation index to correct for bias arising when the number of visitors to a web domain is small (formula referenced in Appendix D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply adjustment to obtain stable estimates; report that findings are similar with the unadjusted index as sensitivity check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel-of-arrival decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify how individuals arrived at news sites into pathways: aggregator (e.g., Google News), direct, social, or search. Compute segregation measures and visit shares separately for each channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare segregation across channels (e.g., social media visits showed higher segregation). Report both segregation statistic and visit share per channel and compare to prior years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation and robustness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform multiple checks: apply alternative raking weights based on political interest; compare aggregate traffic to ComScore; compute isolation index using subsets (top 10 domains 2009 list, 2016 list); use ideology instead of party; compare measures across years (2009, 2013, 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these checks to assess sensitivity to sampling, weighting, domain choice, and measurement choices. Report stability of main patterns across methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking media exposure to attitudinal outcomes (panel analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use two-wave panel survey to measure political attitudes pre- and post-election and link individual-level media diets (audience-based Republican share or content-based conservative slant) to changes in candidate evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute outcome measures as differences favoring Trump over Clinton (feeling thermometer, trait ratings, emotional reactions). Display relationships across quintiles of partisan media exposure and compare slopes between pre- and post-election waves. Note limitations: inability to isolate causal effects and potential pre-treatment crystallization of attitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalization of candidate-evaluation outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate-evaluation outcomes include (a) difference in feeling thermometer assessments of Trump and Clinton, (b) differences in trait ratings (binary coding approach following Gentzkow & Shapiro), and (c) differences in emotional reactions (six emotions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orient outcomes so higher values indicate more favorable assessments of Trump relative to Clinton. Use these to detect whether partisan media diets correspond to change in candidate assessments across survey waves; include regression specifications and robustness checks in appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coder assignment and workload limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each coder in the main analysis labeled at most 200 articles; main analysis uses one coder per article but imposes a cap to limit influence of any single coder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cap reduces dependence on individual coders; combine with pre-test validation and political knowledge quiz to improve quality of crowd-sourced annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of measurement limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly acknowledge potential measurement errors and selection concerns (e.g., low toolbar uptake, coder disagreement about neutrality vs slant, inability to isolate causal effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss possible implications for findings (e.g., attenuation of article-level slant tests, selection bias toward more politically interested panelists) and present analyses demonstrating robustness (alternative weights, validation correlations, aggregate comparisons).
